1.mascotDialogue: An arrow in a directed graph means exactly one thing — you can go this way. Says nothing at all about whether you can come back.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 sets exactly one cell in the matrix. A directed edge only ever writes adjacency[u][v] — never adjacency[v][u].

3.mascotDialogue: Every arrowhead points one way. This particular loop happens to form a cycle, but each edge stays, on her own, one-directional.

4.mascotDialogue: This is the number one most common directed-graph mistake — treating a one-way arrow like she secretly runs both ways. She doesn't. The visual only ever draws the direction you actually set, mate.
